findings.evidence: `rg -n "@\[expose\].*(twoByTwo|twoByTwoId|twoByTwoSwap)|noncomputable def twoByTwo"` hits `StateCardinality.lean:137`, `StateCardinality.lean:142`, and `SmallGridGradings.lean:49`; the same files provide simp characteristic lemmas at lines 149,155,161,167,62,74.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]` from `twoByTwoId`, `twoByTwoSwap`, and `twoByTwo`, and rely on `twoByTwoId_zero`, `twoByTwoId_one`, `twoByTwoSwap_zero`, `twoByTwoSwap_one`, `twoByTwo_O`, and `twoByTwo_X` for downstream use.
findings.issue: `GridState.twoByTwoId`, `GridState.twoByTwoSwap`, and `GridDiagram.twoByTwo` are marked `@[expose]` even though their characteristic simp lemmas provide the public API; exposing these `Classical.choose` bodies leaks implementation details as part of the interface.

findings.evidence: `rg -n "theorem (maslov|alexander).*(: .* = )"` shows these equations at `GradingInteger.lean:128,133` and `SmallGridGradings.lean:145,163,181,186,191,197,204,210,216,221,227,233,239,245`, with no `@[simp]` annotations except unrelated set/marking lemmas.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp]` to the exact grading equations: `maslovOℤ_O`, `maslovXℤ_X`, `maslovXℤ_O_of_two`, `maslovOℤ_X_of_two`, `alexanderTwoℤ_O_of_two`, `alexanderTwoℤ_X_of_two`, `alexander_O_of_two`, `alexander_X_of_two`, and the eight named `twoByTwo` grading lemmas.
findings.issue: The exact normal-form grading lemmas are public but not `@[simp]`, so computations such as `G.maslovOℤ G.O`, `twoByTwo.alexander GridState.twoByTwoId`, and the corresponding `X`/`twoByTwoSwap` values do not simplify automatically.

summary: The public surface exposes choice-based implementation bodies and omits simp annotations on the exact grading normal forms, so downstream users must either unfold implementation details or manually rewrite computations that should simplify.
